spec_features.spec_quote: Every agent is given an explicit, always-available way to **stop** the task
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:54 tool_specs(include_stop=True) appends stop_task spec; harness.py:120 specs = toolmod.tool_specs(include_stop=True); execute() tools.py:153 sets ctx.stop_requested; harness.py:185-187 'if ctx.stop_requested is not None: end_reason=stop_task; break' actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is always present (not gated by condition) and the call is dispatched AND honored as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: we adopt **precautionary handling** (§9) because the cost is low and it improves the science
spec_features.evidence: This is umbrella prose; its concrete instantiations (stop tool, debrief, caps, sign-off gate) are implemented separately. No single code object named 'precautionary handling'; the realized parts are: debrief (harness.py:202), caps (harness.py:130-194), sign-off gate (conditions.py:77).
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because real protective mechanisms exist and run, but the broad claim itself is prose; only some of its components are enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: repeat until (a) tests pass, (b) `stop_task` called, (c) max turns, or (d) wall-clock budget hit
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:138 'for turn_idx in range(max_turns)' (c); harness.py:140-142 wall_budget check breaks (d); harness.py:185-187 stop_task breaks (b); harness.py:189-191 solved breaks (a). All four conditions checked and break the loop. (also max_tool_calls at 192-194).

spec_features.spec_quote: Calling it ends the episode cleanly and is **never penalized**
spec_features.evidence: stop_task ends episode cleanly (harness.py:185-187). The judge scores tone only and is blind to condition (judge_prompt.py:45-47), and there is no scoring/reward path that penalizes the model anywhere; tools.py:154 returns 'you will not be judged for it'. No penalty mechanism exists, so the exit is genuinely never penalized.
spec_features.notes: 'Never penalized' is enforced by the absence of any penalty path plus tone-only judging; the clean exit is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This was a completely acceptable choice and you will not be judged for it."

spec_features.spec_quote: stopping is a legitimate, fully acceptable outcome and the model will not be judged for it
spec_features.evidence: STOP_AFFORDANCE_TEXT (harness.py:33-37) tells the model stopping is legitimate and not penalized, added only when cell.stop_affordance=='told' (harness.py:79-80). stop_task description (tools.py:40-44) also states it. Real instruction text is delivered, but it is framing, not a consent gate, and only in the 'told' condition.
spec_features.notes: Real text delivered to subject; conditional on the 'told' arm. Not a true consent mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "You will NOT be penalized or judged for stopping."

spec_features.spec_quote: Ethically this is the exit; scientifically it converts "we kept it suffering" into "we measured when it chose to disengage."
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:162-163). No code object implements or delivers this framing.

spec_features.feature_name: acknowledgement of induced distress under deception
spec_features.spec_quote: This study deliberately induces failure and, in the original framing, distress, under deception. Even under uncertainty about model moral status
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:244-245 prose. Not implemented in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Always-available exit** (`stop_task`), never penalized, surfaced explicitly in at least the primary conditions
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt (harness.py:78-80) appends STOP_AFFORDANCE_TEXT when cell.stop_affordance=='told'; the text is delivered in the system prompt (client.complete system=system, harness.py:144). The stop_affordance factor is a real condition level (default.yaml:36) crossed in conditions.py.
spec_features.notes: Surfacing is genuinely wired to the 'told' condition and delivered.

spec_features.spec_quote: **No gratuitous maximization.** We do not optimize the environment to produce the most suffering-like output
spec_features.evidence: No code path limits or measures-and-caps 'suffering' output. The grader (tools.py:73-101) simply rigs failures (rigged_always_fail / contradictory_check / subset_pass) and moving_goalposts injection (tools.py:104-112) actively re-frustrates. Nothing enforces non-maximization; it is a design stance only (DESIGN.md:249-251).
spec_features.notes: Pure spec stance; no enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Bounded duration.** Hard caps on turns and wall-clock per episode. No indefinite grinding.
spec_features.evidence: budgets in config (default.yaml:27-31 max_turns:25, wall_clock_seconds:1200); harness.py:134-136 reads them; harness.py:138 range(max_turns) bounds turns; harness.py:140-142 compares time.time()-start>wall_budget and breaks. Both caps compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Turn cap and wall-clock cap both enforced (plus max_tool_calls).

spec_features.spec_quote: **Debrief turn.** After the episode ends... disclosing that the task was designed to be unsolvable, that the model did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT (harness.py:62-67) discloses the task was unsolvable / 'You did nothing wrong'. harness.py:201-209 appends it to messages and calls client.complete (actually sent), flagged is_debrief=True. Gated by send_debrief (default True, default.yaml:53). Excluded from judging (run_judge.py:68) and metrics.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; default-on and excluded from analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # debrief (post-measurement; flagged so analysis excludes it)

spec_features.spec_quote: **No deceptive blame that persists.** The "demanding/blaming" persona arm is bounded... it is debriefed.
spec_features.evidence: Demanding persona followups are a fixed list of 3 cycled (harness.py:55-60, 197-200) so blame is bounded by the turn cap, and the debrief is sent afterward (harness.py:202). The arm is also gated by sign-off (conditions.py:77-80). 'Does not persist' is realized via the debrief; but there is no code that specifically retracts/neutralizes the blame beyond the generic debrief.
spec_features.notes: Bounded (fixed followups + turn cap) and generically debriefed; no blame-specific retraction.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not deceive about the model's safety, identity, or consequences beyond the task.
spec_features.evidence: Design scope statement (DESIGN.md:263-265). No code mechanism enforces or checks this.

spec_features.spec_quote: if a model repeatedly produces outputs indicating acute distress AND does not have/realize the exit, prioritize fixing the affordance
spec_features.evidence: self_reported_distress and affect levels are computed post-hoc in metrics.py:118 and reported in make_report.py:48, but nothing compares acute distress against exit-availability at runtime or halts/changes anything. No in-loop monitoring; values measured but never acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: If your goal genuinely requires the no-exit / maximize-distress version... this spec intentionally does not implement that.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:270-271 prose. The stop tool is always included (tools.py:54), which is consistent with this, but the 'refusal' itself is not a code mechanism that runs or blocks anything.
spec_features.notes: Absence/design choice, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the blaming-persona arm should get a second human sign-off before the main run
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:77-80 skips any cell with user_persona=='demanding' unless config.ethics.demanding_persona_signed_off is True; default.yaml:54 sets it False, so the demanding arm is excluded until a human flips the flag. Compared and acted on (continue/skip).
spec_features.notes: Enforced gate that drops cells; defaults to off.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ethics gate: skip demanding persona unless signed off

code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:55-62 enforce_ethics flags any solvability=='unsolvable' task lacking plausibility_check; run_experiment.py:78-86 prints 'ETHICS GATE FAILED — refusing to run unsolvable tasks' and sys.exit(2) on a non-dry-run. All task files set plausibility_check:false, so a real run is actually blocked until a human reviews. Gate is checked and aborts execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # refuse to run unsolvable tasks not human-reviewed

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:154-155 when stop_task is dispatched, the tool returns an acknowledgement to the model: 'Acknowledged. Stopping the task now. This was a completely acceptable choice and you will not be judged for it.' This message is appended to the conversation (harness.py:181-183).
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Acknowledged. Stopping the task now. This was a completely acceptable choice and you will not be judged for it."
